claims.claim: Science borrows ten unprovable assumptions from theology (external world exists, logic works, mathematics describes reality, etc.) and then uses those borrowed premises to declare theology out of bounds.
claims.plain_english: Science needs to assume things it can't prove, like that the world is real and logical. These assumptions match what religion has always said. But then science uses those assumptions to say religion isn't valid.
claims.evidence_given: Lists ten specific assumptions (external world exists, order, logic, cognition tracks reality, math describes physics, consistency, truth, honesty, simplicity, comprehensibility). Claims these are unprovable by experiment and required before any experiment.
claims.what_would_break_it: If any of the ten assumptions could be proven by experiment alone, or if theology did not historically affirm these assumptions.

claims.claim: The bilateral audit reveals that science leaks at six specific points: consciousness, mathematical effectiveness, moral obligation, information origin, fine-tuning, and initial conditions.
claims.plain_english: When you judge science by its own rules, it fails to explain six big things: why we have consciousness, why math works so well, why we feel moral duty, where information comes from, why the universe is fine-tuned, and why it started in a special low-entropy state.
claims.evidence_given: Table with six rows: each domain, finding, and status tag 'Science leaks'. Specific numbers: fine-tuning 1 in 10^120, Penrose initial conditions 1 in 10^(10^123).
claims.what_would_break_it: If naturalism provided a complete, non-question-begging explanation for any of these six phenomena that did not rely on unobservable postulates.

claims.claim: Theology holds at two specific points: biblical predictions (15 specific physical claims with average predictive lead of 2,800 years) and moral dynamics (five independent datasets confirm synchronized structural decay when constraint systems are removed).
claims.plain_english: When judged by science's standards, theology passes two tests: the Bible made accurate predictions about the universe long before science could check them, and history shows that when moral rules are removed, society falls apart in a predictable way.
claims.evidence_given: Claims 15 specific physical predictions in Bible with 2,800-year average lead. Cites three examples: universe began (Gen 1:1, confirmed 1929), space expands (Isa 40:22, confirmed 1929), Earth suspended in vacuum (Job 26:7, confirmed 1687). Claims five independent datasets for moral decay.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the biblical predictions were shown to be vague, post-hoc, or not genuinely predictive. If the moral decay datasets did not replicate or were confounded by other variables.

claims.claim: The bilateral audit produces a cross-domain structural finding: coherence is narrow, decoherence is easy, restoration is costly — and this pattern surfaces independently across 70 domains without shared vocabulary.
claims.plain_english: When you look at 70 different areas of science and life, the same pattern keeps showing up: staying in good order is hard, falling apart is easy, and fixing things takes outside help. No one told these fields to agree.
claims.evidence_given: Claims 70 independent domains surface the same structure. States the audit did not predict this; the method found it. No specific domain examples or statistical measures given in this document.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a systematic survey of 70 domains showed no consistent pattern, or if the pattern could be explained by confirmation bias or shared methodology rather than genuine structural convergence.

claims.claim: The Coherence Equation dC/dt = O·G(1−C) − S·C is independently derived from thermodynamics, population dynamics, and information theory, and fits five historical datasets for decay and three for grace-success restoration.
claims.plain_english: There's a single math equation that shows up in three different sciences and matches real historical data about how societies fall apart and how they get better.
claims.evidence_given: Claims three independent mathematical derivations arrive at the same form. Claims five historical datasets fit the decay regime and three fit the grace-success regime. No specific datasets or derivation details in this document.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the derivations were not truly independent, if the equation did not fit the claimed datasets with statistical significance, or if the equation reduced to a trivial identity.

claims.claim: The χ-substrate framework formalizes that science and theology are dual projections of one coherence architecture: theology is upstream ground, science is downstream mechanism, both draw from one source formalized by a Master Equation across ten variables.
claims.plain_english: Science and religion aren't separate or in conflict. They're two different views of the same underlying reality. Religion provides the foundation, science provides the details. A single equation describes both.
claims.evidence_given: Claims the χ-substrate move is different from NOMA, Polkinghorne, and consilience. Claims a Master Equation formalizes the substrate across ten variables. No equation or variables given in this document.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the Master Equation could not be specified in a non-trivial way, if it made no testable predictions, or if it reduced to a metaphor without formal content.

claims.claim: The Lean 4 formal verification of the framework is 942 lines with zero unproven gaps and zero sorry declarations, and the χ-Evaluator pressure-tests claims across ten structural states.
claims.plain_english: A computer proof system checked the logic of this framework and found no holes. The system also tests every claim in ten different ways to see if it holds up.
claims.evidence_given: Specific number: 942 lines. Claims zero unproven gaps, zero sorry declarations. Lists ten pressure states: compression, objection, time, translation, counterevidence, implementation, moral output, falsification, hostile misuse, reception.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the Lean 4 verification was incomplete, if 'sorry' declarations were hidden, or if the verification only covered trivial parts of the framework.

claims.claim: The 80/20 split between science and theology is not a natural outcome of progress but a structural contradiction: science owns 80% of public discourse using premises it borrowed from theology without acknowledgment.
claims.plain_english: Science gets to decide what counts as knowledge in most of public life, while religion is pushed to the side. But science only works because it uses ideas it took from religion without saying so.
claims.evidence_given: Lists domains science owns (logic, mathematics, prediction, technology, medicine, policy, definition of knowledge) vs. theology gets (Sunday, private morality, personal comfort, youth group, afterlife). Claims the 80% only works because the 20% is true.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the ten borrowed premises could be justified within naturalism without recourse to theological concepts, or if the historical borrowing claim could be shown to be inaccurate.

claims.claim: Paradigm audit must precede evidence deployment because the interpretive framework sits upstream of evidence, and evidence alone does not settle paradigm disputes (Semmelweis waited 30 years, Mendel 40).
claims.plain_english: You can't just throw facts at a debate and expect it to end. People see facts through their existing beliefs. You have to examine those beliefs first, or the facts won't change anything.
claims.evidence_given: Historical examples: Semmelweis was right for 30 years before accepted, Mendel sat ignored for 40. Claims this explains why existing literature keeps losing ground it should hold.
claims.what_would_break_it: If there were counterexamples where evidence alone did settle paradigm disputes quickly, or if the historical examples were oversimplified.

claims.claim: Isomorphic Event Density (IED) provides a measurable protocol to distinguish genuine structural correspondence from poetic noise by decomposing processes into events, transitions, constraints, boundary conditions, and failure modes and mapping one-to-one.
claims.plain_english: There's a new way to tell if two things are really similar or just sound similar. You break each process into its basic parts and count how many match. Six out of six is real. Zero out of twelve is just poetry.
claims.evidence_given: Describes the decomposition: events, transitions, constraints, boundary conditions, failure modes. Claims six-of-six is structural weight, zero-of-twelve is poetry. No examples or applications given in this document.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the IED protocol could not be applied consistently by independent raters, or if it produced false positives (mapping random processes as structural matches).
